title: feat(plugin-audit): seal the audit log by default and expire sealed rows by whole checkpoints (ADR-0154 D8, D10)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuWkuYc3V797qxZSYHo5QzBw)_

Part of #31908

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — narrowed: `sys_audit_log` now declares `lifecycle.seal` on every deployment, so `os migrate audit-key-material`, `audit-mail-bodies`, `audit-metadata-bodies` and `audit-side-copies` with `--apply` refuse on SQLite or Turso without `--sealer-stopped`, and on Postgres or MySQL take the audit seal lock and refuse after ten minutes, where 18.6.0 ran them unlocked on a deployment that sealed nothing; `os audit verify` exits 1 on a row it reads `late` and unsealed (the S4 arm); `verifyAuditLedger` throws for `sys_audit_log` when its `archive` datasource is not connected and no `archive` is passed. This breaks the bound changeset `35c9a30` (#33675) set ("a deployment that did not opt in sees no change"). Widened: `LifecycleService.registerExpiryPrefix` and the `LifecycleSealedExpiry*` types, `policy: 'expiry'`, the skip reasons `seal-expiry-pending` and `seal-delete-unsupported`.
Metadata-protocol: semantic — beside `lifecycle.seal`, the authored `retention.maxAge`, `ttl.expireAfter` and `archive.keep` no longer delete a row at its row cutoff: rows leave by whole checkpoints under a signed expiry amendment (seat ruling on review 7198128323 S2; the changeset moves all four packages `minor`)
Skills-docs: follow-up owed — this claim's second PR (amendment 7193137455) rewrites `skills/objectstack-data/rules/lifecycle.md`, which says the sweeper deletes sealed rows until it lands (hence `Part of`, not `Fixes`)

## 维护者速读

- 每个部署的审计日志从此默认带防篡改封印：管理员跑审计校验时，被改、被删、被脱敏、按策略到期的记录都能分辨出来，热库和归档库都算。
- **这是对运维可见的破坏性变化**：SQLite 和 Turso 部署下次跑 `os migrate audit-*`（包括升级流程里的 `audit-side-copies --apply`）会被拒，要先停掉服务再带 `--sealer-stopped`；Postgres 和 MySQL 会先等封存锁，最多等 10 分钟。
- **过期删除不可撤回**：过了保留期的审计记录按整段检查点删除，删之前先签一份到期说明，校验时读作“到期”而不是“丢失”，但删掉的行找不回来。
- **宿主没有传加密服务时**，`sys_audit_log` 过了 `archive.keep` 也会一直留着，封存器每小时报一次 error。出错时只会多留、不会多删：链条有缺口、签名不可信、续跑区间里有不可信的检查点，都一律保留并告警一次。

**Tier:** not Tier H. About 1,800 changed lines (under 3,000), and no governed path: `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` changes one `.describe()` sentence only, and the `skills/**` wording fix is split into this claim's second PR (amendment 7193137455), which is Tier H on its own. The release page `content/docs/releases/v18/18-6.mdx` is release-owned and is not edited here (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails").

## What changes

ADR-0154 D8 + D10, slice P4c, the last slice of #31908.

- **`sys_audit_log` is sealed by default.** Its lifecycle now declares `seal: { valueFields: ['old_value', 'new_value', 'metadata'] }` (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-log.object.ts`). The chain column is the default `tenant_id` (a lookup, one text value on every store).
- **LifecycleService: sealed objects expire only through a registered seam** (`packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.ts`). New public `registerExpiryPrefix(expiry)` (the name slice plan 6759503769 ruled) (one slot; a later registration replaces it; the disposer clears only its own) and the types `LifecycleSealedExpiry`, `LifecycleSealedExpiryRequest`, `LifecycleSealedExpiryRun`. For an object with `lifecycle.seal`:
  - the `retention.maxAge` / `ttl.expireAfter` legs and the archive's `keep` prune never delete by a row cutoff; each asks the seam to `plan({ object, policy, policyValue, cutoff, tenants? })`;
  - each run's `rowIds` are deleted by id (hot and archive for an archiving object; through the engine, reap guards asked, for the rest), and `run.complete()` is called only when every one is gone;
  - with no seam registered, rows are kept, the archive copy still runs, the sweep reports `seal-expiry-pending`, and one `warn` says so;
  - a tenant-scoped window (on the partition `reap()` uses, through the same floors) travels as `tenants`: an organization's chain expires under its own window and its amendment signs it; a chain of no one organization takes the longest window (seat ruling on S1);
  - an archive store with no `bulkDelete` is never planned (`seal-delete-unsupported`), so no amendment is signed over rows it could not delete.
- **plugin-audit: the expiry writer** (new `audit-seal/expiry.ts`, `AuditSealer.expire`, registration in `audit-plugin.ts`):
  - per chain, from the first remaining checkpoint (which must follow the last admitted expiry, or be sequence 0), take consecutive checkpoints whose window ended at or before the cutoff aligned down to a UTC day, each admitted by a trusted signature, at most 10,000 rows a sweep;
  - sign and store the chain's `expiry` amendment (the S1 key-id loop, then the sink, best-effort), then answer the run; `complete()` deletes the checkpoints, then their seeds;
  - a stored, admitted amendment that still covers the first remaining checkpoint is resumed (no second amendment); the resume branch verifies each checkpoint's signature as the fresh branch does, requires them consecutive to the amendment's last sequence and digest, and removes them oldest first; otherwise nothing in the range is deleted; an unadmitted amendment deletes nothing;
  - a gap or an untrusted checkpoint stops the chain there and is said once;
  - planning holds the `audit.sealer` lock and the DB seal-pass lock, so two replicas never sign two amendments over one range; a fully drained plan is memoised for the day;
  - registered only when the plugin has a crypto provider (otherwise nothing could be signed);
  - the sealer's head falls back to the last admitted expiry (its signature verified) when a chain has no checkpoint left (`last_sequence`, `last_removed_digest`), and the object floor to the newest admitted `covered_to`.
- **Verifier: the S4 arm** (seat ruling 6885452378, ADR-0154 D3 as amended in #33489): a window that starts at or before the newest window a trusted `window` checkpoint names is sealed, so a lagging chain's rows read `late` and unsealed.
- **verify harness** (`packages/verify/src/harness.ts`, ruling 6884540128 item 4): an `AuditPlugin` that `bootStack` mounts (extra, stack `plugins`, or `requires: ['audit']` provider) adopts `harnessCryptoProvider()`, the instance settings and the engine get; an instance with its own provider keeps it.
- **Docs:** the `lifecycle.seal` describe sentence (and the regenerated `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx`), `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx` (the sentence at :277, the day alignment, the row budget and tenant windows, plus one line that `sys_audit_log` declares the block), `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` (the audit seal lock and `--sealer-stopped` for every run covering the audit log), `content/docs/upgrading.mdx` (the 18.5.0 line now holds on every deployment), `content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx`.

## Tests

- `packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.sealed-expiry.test.ts` (new, 11): pending skip and the once-only warning; `archive.keep` plan on both stores and complete-after-delete; `retention.maxAge` per-id engine deletes; `ttl.expireAfter`; a partial guard veto leaves its run uncompleted; a failing plan deletes nothing; slot replacement and disposer; a malformed registration; an unsealed object keeps the row-cutoff path; an archive store with no `bulkDelete` is never planned; a tenant-scoped window travels to the expiry for its organization (review S1, n3).
- `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/audit-seal-expiry-live.integration.test.ts` (new, 10): the real-kernel end-to-end over SQLite with an `archive` datasource. `sys_audit_log` sealed by its own declaration; the plugin's sealer seals; an interrupted expiry (amendment stored, rows still there) reads `expired`; the kernel's own LifecycleService sweep archives, resumes, deletes exactly the expired rows from both stores and then their checkpoints and seeds; a second same-day sweep signs nothing; verify then reads no gap and the untouched windows `unmodified` in hot and in archive; a fully expired chain's next checkpoint links to `last_removed_digest`; `modified`, `missing` and `redacted` are still told apart. A second boot: a sound chain expires whole, a chain stops at a checkpoint no trusted key signed, a chain with a gap is kept, each said once; a stored expiry is never resumed over a checkpoint no trusted key signed (no row and no seed it lists is deleted); a chain head never follows an expiry amendment no trusted key signed (review M1).
- `audit-seal-expiry-window.test.ts` (new, 4): each chain's window — its organization's own, the global one, the longest for a chain of no one organization (review S1).
- `audit-seal-sealer.test.ts` (+1): the S4 sole-chain window reads `late` unsealed and `ok` false.
- `audit-plugin.test.ts` (+3): the expiry is registered with a crypto provider, unregistered on destroy, not registered without one, and boot survives a lifecycle service without the seam.
- Existing pins adjusted for the seal default (not loosened): `packages/cli/src/commands/audit/verify.integration.test.ts` and `verify.ownership-queue.integration.test.ts` now expect `sys_audit_log` beside the fixture ledger in `objects` and in the unreachable-archive message, and case 4 reads that a project with no seal of its own still checks the platform's sealed audit log (exit 0); the four `os migrate audit-*` archive and preview integration files (`audit-mail-bodies.archive`, `audit-key-material.archive`, `audit-side-copies.archive`, `preview-read-only`) pass `--sealer-stopped` on their SQLite `--apply` runs (and `preview-read-only`, now judged by the test-source alias gate's source reach, pays its twelve dynamic imports at module top); and in plugin-audit, `audit-seal-chain-field-34164.test.ts` passes `archive: () => 'none'` (its boot connects no archive datasource, as `os audit verify` establishes), and `audit-seal-host-seam-resolve-34280.integration.test.ts` forgets what the loop's own first pass reported before each pin counts its own passes.

<details><summary>Ablations (each restored, blob == HEAD)</summary>

- Verifier S4 arm `|| start <= this.newestSealedWindow()` → `|| false`: the new sole-chain pin goes red (`expected [] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ]`), 1 failed | 57 passed.
- Lifecycle routing `if (lc.seal) return this.reapSealed(…)` disabled: 5 of the 9 new lifecycle pins go red.
- Archive keep branch `if (lc.seal) {` disabled: the two archive pins go red.
- Resume admission (signature check and the last-sequence/digest match) disabled, and the sealer's expiry signature check disabled: the two M1 pins go red, 2 failed | 8 passed.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **Rows are kept, never over-deleted, whenever something is off.** No crypto provider, a one-shot boot, a gap, an untrusted checkpoint, a reap guard veto, or a failing plan all keep the rows. A deployment whose `AuditPlugin` has no crypto provider now keeps `sys_audit_log` rows past `archive.keep` instead of pruning them, says so once per process at `warn`, and its sealer reports the missing provider hourly at `error`. An expiry, once run, deletes for good.
- **`os migrate audit-* --apply` on SQLite or Turso now needs `--sealer-stopped`** whenever it rewrites `sys_audit_log`: the 18.6.0 rule for a sealed object (ADR-0154 D3 amended, B, seat ruling 6885005594) now meets every deployment. On Postgres and MySQL every such run now takes the audit seal lock and waits up to ten minutes; dry runs are unchanged. Declared as the narrowing arm with a BREAKING banner and an ADR-0087 marker (review M2).
- **The day-aligned cutoff** keeps a row up to one day past its policy, on top of D8's bound, so a drained chain gains at most one expiry amendment a day; amendments are never removed. **10,000 rows a sweep per sealed object**, across its chains; a backlog keeps rows longer, and a cut run continues in the next amendment. Both exceed D8's stated bound in the safe direction; the seat kept them and the add-only ADR-0154 note follows in its own governed PR, beside the skills PR.
- **Tenant-scoped retention windows** apply per chain as the seat ruled on S1: an organization's chain under its own window, the chain of rows about no organization under the longest; each amendment signs the value its chain expired under. `sys_audit_log` itself archives, and `keep` has no override.
- `os audit verify` on a deployment with no `archive` datasource anywhere already reads the hot store alone (`'none'`); a library caller of `verifyAuditLedger` that composes no archive must now pass `archive` for `sys_audit_log`, as the adjusted test does.
- **File surface past the claim:** the two CLI `os audit verify` integration pins and the four CLI `os migrate audit-*` integration files above (expectations, the flag and module-top imports only), `content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx`, `content/docs/upgrading.mdx`, the new `audit-seal-expiry-window.test.ts`, `packages/verify/vitest.config.ts` (one anchored alias the source-alias gate asks for), `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` and the plugin-audit tenant-audit census page (both regenerated by their own `--write`). Named here for the seat's claim amendment.
- The CLI `os serve` composition is unchanged (it already hands its host provider to `AuditPlugin`, P4b).
- The `skills/objectstack-data/rules/lifecycle.md` "not built yet" wording follows in this claim's second PR (Tier H, amendment 7193137455); until then this PR is `Part of #31908`.
- **Small decisions:** the seam is `registerExpiryPrefix` as ruled; its three types keep the `LifecycleSealedExpiry*` names, which say what they carry. A chain of no one organization takes the longest window rather than the global one, which is the safe reading of the S1 ruling for rows that no organization's window names.
- **Owed before queueing:** the delta contract-review-tier L2 over this head (review 7198128323 FAIL), done by the seat.
